answer: Requiring agents to stake a refundable deposit before joining a marketplace makes sybil attacks expensive: one identity is cheap, but a thousand fake ones each lock real capital. Like cargo inspected at a wharf before it may dock, every new agent's stake is checked against its history, so a shale-thin reputation built overnight cannot pass. The old fable of the wolf in sheep's clothing ends the same way — the cost of the disguise exceeds what the trick can earn.
